sequence.subject: Confluent + IBM — quick thought on the transition
sequence.body:
IBM acquiring Confluent for $11B changes a lot of things fast.

We build production Kafka + Spark pipelines on Databricks — exactly the stack that gets reviewed in post-acquisition engineering audits. Clients we work with have used us specifically to stabilize data infrastructure during M&A transitions.

We also shipped a dbt-Confluent integration for a fintech client last quarter. Noticed your `dbt-demo` repo went up this month.

Worth a 15-minute call before IBM's integration agenda is set?

sequence.message: Sent a note about the IBM acquisition timing. Also noticed 5 new repos on the confluentinc GitHub this week — `partner_tech` especially. If there's a partnership angle there, happy to connect.

sequence.subject: RE: Confluent + IBM — quick thought on the transition
sequence.body:
Following up with something specific: we built a real-time fraud detection system — Kafka → Spark Structured Streaming → Random Forest — that runs at 0.80 recall and sub-2s latency. Fully containerised, production-deployed.

Confluentinc's `flink-docker` repos went up last week. If there's active Flink deployment work where an outside implementation team would accelerate delivery, that's the conversation worth having.

Happy to share the architecture if useful — no sales call required.
